claims: SQ99 out-of-corpus transfer of the E1-vs-E0 gap (exploratory; no ledger row yet)
prediction: Written 2026-11-22 before any SQ99 run; EXPLORATORY: single-seed v0.3.0 checkpoints (E0, E1) at an untuned LR (Phase 2b E10 / E1 at tuned LRs are re-run later via --checkpoint). (1) Out-of-corpus bits/char is much higher than in-corpus clean-val bits/char for BOTH models: ratio > 1.5x (E0 clean-val is about 0.28 per K9, so out-of-corpus > 0.42; format shift from synthetic prompt+solution docs to raw library files, plus content shift, plus no near-duplicates). (2) E1 still beats E0 out of corpus (gap = bpc(E1)/bpc(E0) - 1 < 0), but by LESS than its in-corpus clean-val gap (|gap_out| < |gap_in|), because part of the in-corpus advantage may come from memorising near-duplicates (the hybrid has a smaller attention footprint but a recurrent state that compresses seen text well). (3) The ordering is the same on every source with >= 15 docs, up to noise.
criterion: Primary: 'the hybrid advantage TRANSFERS' if the out-of-corpus gap bpc(E1)/bpc(E0) - 1 is < 0 AND its 95% paired per-doc bootstrap CI (BCa, B=10,000, same docs for both models) excludes 0 (upper end < 0); 'DOES NOT TRANSFER' if the CI includes 0 or the gap is >= 0. Second readout (reported, not gating): 'SIMILAR SIZE' if gap_out / gap_in lies in [0.5, 1.5] with gap_in the in-corpus clean-val gap measured through the same CPU scorer on a token-matched sample (otherwise 'SMALLER' / 'LARGER' / 'n/a' when gap_in >= 0). Prediction readouts (reported, not gating): out/in bits/char ratio > 1.5 for both models; |gap_out| < |gap_in|. Caveats stored with the result: the two sets differ in document format and length (raw library files vs prose+code problems), so 'out of corpus' is confounded with format shift; single seed; untuned LR; the CPU path is fp32 with a reference GDN, not the bf16 fla path the models were trained on.
